items.title: Shein finally goes public. Now comes the harder test
items.excerpt: Key takeaways Shein s advantage comes from testing tiny product batches and scaling winners quickly , not simply from selling cheap clothes. New tariffs, parcel fees and regulation are making that model more expensive and harder to reproduce across markets. Inditex and H M show why brand, inventory discipline and distribution can matter more than pure speed. Shein taught fashion to behave a little like a social-media feed: test something, watch the reaction, then produce more of what people click on. On 1 September 2026, the China-founded, Singapore-headquartered retailer finally reached the Hong Kong stock market after failed attempts to list in New York and London. items.title: Higher oil = higher energy? It’s not that simple
items.excerpt: Key points: Energy is becoming more relevant in portfolios again. Middle East disruption has revived the role of energy as a geopolitical and inflation hedge, while Venezuela shows how the global supply map can also evolve. Energy is not one trade. Oil producers, refiners, pipelines, LNG, power generators and grid companies sit at different points of the value chain and respond to very different drivers. The longer-term opportunity is broadening beyond traditional hydrocarbons. EVs challenge road-fuel demand, but AI, electrification, LNG, nuclear and grid investment are creating another energy investment cycle. items.title: Euro FX futures hold near 1.1650 as CVOL ticks higher.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures traded near unchanged on Thursday, hovering around the 1.1650 level after drifting lower from last week's highs above 1.17. The market continues to take its cues from U.S. Dollar strength, even as expectations remain for a 25 bps rate hike from the European Central Bank next month. Volatility steadily edged higher throughout the week, reflected in the CVOL index, as traders position themselves for the Jackson Hole economic symposium. Friday's session will bring additional data points, including the Chicago Purchasing Managers index and University of Michigan sentiment, though market attention remains squarely on the scheduled 9:00 a.m. address from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

items.title: Euro FX futures slide as inflation data supports dollar.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures experience a near-term pullback following their late August cycle high, navigating a mix of U.S. inflation figures and supportive European economic data. Core PCE in the U.S. held firm at 3.3% year-over-year, keeping higher-for-longer interest rate debates active and providing underlying support for the dollar. Conversely, the euro finds some domestic strength as August PMI figures reflect improving manufacturing conditions, led by Germany. Additionally, German second-quarter GDP saw an upward revision to 0.3%, potentially easing recessionary fears and providing the European Central Bank with flexibility to maintain restrictive policy.

PCE inflation and second-quarter GDP both match expectations, keeping the Federal Reserve's rate path in focus ahead of key Jackson Hole speeches. In energy, crude oil breaks below $80 as U.S. sanctions and a blockade drive a sharp drop in Iranian exports, despite ongoing diplomatic mediation. Plus, a look ahead at upcoming Treasury auctions, key tech earnings and jobless claims data.
